reasons: Classification is correct: § 10 is mutual with a reasonable-consent standard, but it requires Contractor consent for every transfer, including to a Company affiliate or an M&A successor. The playbook fallback expressly requires a right to assign to successors on written notice, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term rather than merely falling short of preferred wording.

The redline is valid and additive: it preserves the existing mutual consent sentence and appends a proviso giving Company an affiliate/successor carve-out, which is the edit the redline guidance calls for. The 0.630 changed-character ratio reflects the length of the appended proviso relative to a short clause, not a rewrite — no original language was altered or deleted.

Rationale is accurate on the change-of-control leg: no CoC trigger exists (§ 6 termination limited to convenience with no open SOW and uncured material breach), so no deletion was needed, and omitting the 'no assignment to a Customer competitor' restriction is correctly characterized as a preferred-position refinement noted rather than flagged.
Comment matches the redline, is concise, cites the playbook position, and offers the mutual notice-based fallback as an alternative; no double-flagging of the same term under another rule.
